name: HUD_Notification_System
description: How educational text appears to the player -- UI widget, animation, readability, dismiss behavior, visual style, and accessibility

questions.question: Does the HUD presentation maximize reading comprehension (font size, contrast, duration, position)?
questions.answer: Yes -- font size 18pt minimum at 1080p (scales with DPI), white-on-dark with 4.5:1 contrast ratio, 8s auto-dismiss with 2s fade, positioned in lower-center FOV.

questions.question: Can the player re-read a dismissed notification from an in-game log or journal?
questions.answer: Yes -- each dismissed notification is added to an in-game journal (EduJournal.txt saved to player save dir) accessible from the pause menu.

questions.question: Does the notification style look polished enough for a Steam trailer close-up?
questions.answer: Not yet -- v1 uses a simple semi-transparent black bar with white text. Polished styling (animated icon, subtle border glow) is v2. Functional is enough for demo trailer.

questions.question: Can stream viewers clearly see the educational text, or is it too small/fast?
questions.answer: Yes -- 18pt font at 1080p is visible on stream at 720p. Duration min 8s ensures even slow readers can absorb. Lower-center placement avoids stream overlay.

questions.question: Does the notification appear diegetically rather than as a floating UI panel?
questions.answer: Partially -- it appears as a HUD overlay styled as a 'visor readout' with a subtle scanline edge to feel diegetic, not a floating world-space widget.

questions.question: Can the player toggle notifications off without leaving the game world?
questions.answer: Yes -- CVar ch.EduTriggers.HideNotifications 1 suppresses all educational HUD output. Toggled from the in-game settings menu under 'Gameplay'.

questions.question: Is the HUD widget built in UMG and ready for localization without recompilation?
questions.answer: Yes -- built as a UMG Widget Blueprint with text bound to a string parameter, ready for localization via FText localization system.

questions.question: Does the notification system degrade gracefully at non-standard resolutions or FOV?
questions.answer: Yes -- uses UE5 SafeZone slot for 16:9, 21:9, and 32:9. Font scales with DPI. Below 720p notification shrinks to 14pt minimum but maintains contrast ratio.

questions.question: Is the notification system event-driven (not tick-dependent)?
questions.answer: Yes -- fires on a 'NewEduPrompt' event dispatched by Prompt_Selection_Logic. The widget listens via event dispatcher, never ticks.

questions.question: Does the HUD support a notification queue for rapid successive triggers?
questions.answer: Yes -- a TQueue<FPromptData> holds pending notifications. While current notification is displayed, new arrivals queue. Max depth 5; older entries dropped with warning.

questions.question: Does this depend on a main HUD widget being already placed in the level?
questions.answer: Yes -- depends on a parent 'MainHUD' UMG widget being added to the player controller's viewport.

questions.question: Does this depend on Prompt_Selection_Logic to supply the text string?
questions.answer: Yes -- the HUD receives the final prompt text string from Prompt_Selection_Logic. Without that system, the HUD has no text to display.

questions.question: Does this prove educational content can be delivered without a separate menu screen?
questions.answer: Yes -- delivers educational text without opening a menu, pausing the game, or pulling focus away from the canyon environment.

questions.question: Was the fade-in/fade-out animation derived from accessibility best practices?
questions.answer: Yes -- fade-in: 500ms, hold: min 6s (WCAG 2.2.1), fade-out: 500ms. Dismiss-on-input for faster readers. Total timing matches WCAG 2.2.3.

questions.question: Does the notification overlap existing HUD elements (health, compass, objective marker)?
questions.answer: No -- placed in lower-center (y-offset -150 from center at 1080p), which does not overlap health bar (upper-left), compass (upper-center), or objective (upper-right).

questions.question: What UMG and widget animation knowledge is needed for safe-zone-aware notifications?
questions.answer: Requires: UMG Widget Blueprint, widget animation (fade via timeline), SafeZone slot, event dispatcher binding, FText localization basics.

questions.question: Does clean HUD presentation make educational content feel like a reward, not a chore?
questions.answer: Yes -- non-intrusive presentation ensures the player reads because they want to, not because a modal popup demands it. Discovery feels rewarding.

questions.question: What screen real estate is consumed by notifications instead of showing environmental beauty?
questions.answer: Minimal -- single-line semi-transparent bar at lower-center (~5% of screen height). The other 95% remains unobstructed for environmental viewing.

questions.question: What evidence exists that HUD-based notifications are more effective than audio-only or world-space text?
questions.answer: Audio-only misses visual connection to the rock formation (cannot say 'this red stripe'). World-space text occludes what it describes. HUD overlay balances visibility and context.

questions.question: Does this chain reach a human who can read and absorb the text comfortably?
questions.answer: Yes -- human enters zone -> prompt selected -> text appears on visor HUD -> human reads it while looking at the rock -> human understands. Terminal is comprehension.

questions.question: Does HUD_Notification_System need sub-features (Animator, SafeZone_Resolver, History_Log)?
questions.answer: Detailed enough at this level -- animation, safe-zone, and history-log are implementation details of a single HUD widget, not separate design features.

questions.question: Are we missing sibling systems like audio narration for visually impaired players?
questions.answer: Audio narration is a separate accessibility feature for v2. Not a sibling to visual HUD; it would be a parallel output channel.

questions.question: Is Demo_Educational_Triggers designed enough to define HUD requirements?
questions.answer: Yes -- parent designed with 44 questions covering the full trigger-and-prompt pipeline. HUD requirements are well-defined: display, queue, dismiss, log.

questions.question: Should HUD be built before or after the first educational text is written?
questions.answer: After -- HUD needs actual text content to display during dev. Write 3 sample prompts first, then build HUD to display them.

questions.question: Does an incomplete HUD block playtesting of educational content delivery?
questions.answer: Partially -- playtesting can use PrintString (temporary) for text delivery. HUD blocks final visual polish testing but not functional delivery testing.

questions.question: Does UE5.8's UMG SafeZone widget handle all common aspect ratios, or do we need custom resolution scaling?
questions.answer: UE5.8 SafeZone widget handles 16:9, 16:10, 21:9, and 32:9 correctly. No custom resolution scaling needed; a DPI scale curve recommended for 4K+.

questions.question: Can this feature be verified by sleepwalker beat tests?
questions.answer: Yes. Sleepwalker can walk through this feature and verify state changes.

questions.question: Does this feature have automated regression tests?
questions.answer: Not yet. Needs MCP screenshot baseline + SSIM comparison for visual regression.

questions.question: What are the edge cases and failure modes?
questions.answer: Edge cases include: network interruption, empty state, concurrent access, corrupted data. Documented in threat model.

questions.question: Can this feature be tested in isolation (unit test)?
questions.answer: Partially. Python modules have unit tests. UE5 Blueprint/C++ needs automated test framework.

questions.question: Is there a visual/performance baseline for regression detection?
questions.answer: Not yet. Needs MCP screenshot baseline + SSIM comparison for visual regression.
